newsitem.title: ZAIRE: 33 dead as East Zaire factions clash.
newsitem.headline: 33 dead as East Zaire factions clash.

text.p: At least 11 people were killed in rebel-held East Zaire on Friday in fighting between factions of the alliance of rebel forces, eyewitnesses said.
Mai-Mai fighters attacked Banyamulenge troops at Butembo 180 -km (112-miles) north of Goma on Friday morning.
"Five Mai-Mai rebels were killed and six or seven civilians also died," according to an eyewitness.
Zairean Red Cross officials said after the battle they picked up several bodies with grass woven into their hair, a sign they were Mai-Mai fighters.
The Mai-Mai, who believe bullets fired at them will turn to water, spearheaded rebel advances but the child warriors among them have refused orders from rebel officers.

On Wednesday 22 people including 15 civilians were killed in clashes in Butembo the eyewitnesses said and similar clashes were reported near Bunia, 360-km (220-miles) north of Goma, seized by rebels last week.
Butembo was tense late on Friday with Banyamulenge troops taking up strategic positions across the town.
Analysts said the fighting provides the first hard evidence of a split between factions of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire led by Laurent Kabila.
Kabila said last week he was disarming the Mai-Mai and sending them to training camps because they raped and brutalised civilians.
The Alliance seized control of a swathe of East Zaire from the government army in October and November dislodging hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees in the process.
Banyamulenge rebels who come from South Kivu contracted the North Kivu Mai-Mai during the war as front-line fighters and defenders of territory taken by rebels.
But aid workers said in December tensions between the two groups strained the Alliance, with Mai-Mai fighters unwilling to cede territory they had captured.
Zaire's newly-formed crisis government told the army on Friday to mount a "total and devastating" offensive to retake the lost border territory from the rebels.
